recommendation._scope: A measurement verdict is NOT a production admission. The owner decisions in docs/BASE_MAINNET_CUSTODY_ADJUDICATION.md section 10 remain the owner's; this block recommends with numbers and decides nothing.

section10item6.question: Whether the new generation accepts a null verifier when requirePq == false

variantA_keepRequirement.genesisCost: one permissionless deployVerifier(attestor) call on the Generation root, by anyone, once per attestor address; the verifier is never consulted while requirePq == false

variantB_acceptNull.newKernelState: pqVerifier == address(0) becomes a reachable state every later edge must refuse (setVerifier and initiateRecovery do today)

section10item6.recommended: KEEP THE REQUIREMENT (variant A): the null variant is 57 bytes LARGER, refuting the 'dropping it saves bytes' hypothesis, and buys only the omission of a permissionless call that costs no authority.

recommendation.safestAdmission: Only an asset with vanilla ERC-20 transfer semantics (exact debit, no fee, no rebasing, no hooks); a recipient-leg fee is the one behaviour no sender-side settlement rule can observe. The admission is a property of the ASSET, decided by the owner, not of the kernel.
